P1: Asserts 20¢, 'Holding Carrot ×1', size 6 and carrot stock >= 1. It starts the game with __GROW.newGame(seed), not the Play button.
P2: Movement goes through __GROW.keyDown('KeyD') plus __GROW.advance(), which writes the key map directly; no keyboard event is ever dispatched. It asserts movement and that two runs match. I confirmed the real keys work myself.
P3: Planting is __GROW.tap('KeyE'), which calls Sim.actE directly instead of pressing E. The stage 0 / empty hand / stage 2 at 10 s / ripe at 20 s assertions are correct.
P4: Harvest is tap('KeyE'), not a key press. The R4 value check runs on the plant's fruit before harvest; afterwards it checks only that the backpack count is 1, not the item.
P5: Deliver uses a real click on #btn-deliver and asserts the purse rose by fruit value + 30 (20 to 74).
P6: Buy uses a real click on 'Buy Carrot'. It plants, waters at 4 s, then checks not ripe at 15 s, ripe at exactly 16, can 2, and refill 3 (the gardener is 2 m from the barrel, so no walk is needed). Plant, water and refill go through the tap API.
P7: Saves mid-game, restores in a second chromium.launch() process, advances 30 s, and compares canonical dumps. The original side is also a restore of the blob, not the live state, but my own live-vs-fresh check was equal too.
P8: The proof compares load(+1h) with load plus one advance(3600). Both are the same catchUp call, so the check is close to a tautology rather than 'playing the hour through'. My 1/60 s stepped play matched every outcome, with timestamp float differences of about 1e-11.
P9: +100 and Skip 1 hour are clicked through the UI. It reports 2.7 ms at 101 plants and 5.5 ms at 1,082. The number is CPU time of the synchronous redraw, not presented frames.
P10: All nine PNGs were rewritten by the rerun. The night and rain shots use a presentation preview override (setPreview), not real game time or weather. planted.png hides the sprout under the prompt pills.

look: The HUD layout is a close match to the reference: top-left chips, top-right buttons, market panel top-right, care panel bottom-right, centred prompt stack, Move and E buttons. The world uses the art kit with the stall, path, fence and lanterns. The renders are darker and more saturated than the reference's bright pastel flat lighting. The camera is closer and lower, so tree canopies are cut off at the top and the right of the garden is clipped. The prompt pills sit on the gardener's feet, and the cask is recoloured blue.
summary: The simulation is faithful to the brief: every rule number and formula checks out in code and in my own runs, and the real game plays end to end with keyboard and mouse, including the camera following the gardener out to the 20 m bound and offline catch-up from the real localStorage save. What is missing is in the proof rather than the game: it never dispatches a keyboard event (movement, E, Q and R go through a window.__GROW test API that calls the simulation), and its P8 offline check compares two identical catch-up calls instead of stepped play. What is wrong is mostly the look: darker and more saturated lighting than the reference, a tighter camera that crops the trees and the garden, and prompt pills that cover the gardener.
